chunks: Safwan narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Maghrib and 'Isha prayers are combined with one Adhan and two Iqamas; do not pray anything in between them.
And he said: 'Thus the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed.'
ai.seo_question: How are the Maghrib and Isha prayers combined according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the specific procedural method for Jam' al-Qasr (combining shortening prayers), requiring a single Adhan followed by two distinct Iqamas for Maghrib and 'Isha. It underscores the continuity of this practice with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), reinforcing the validity of the single-Adhan tradition in Shia fiqh. The prohibition of intervening prayers ensures the structural integrity of the combined unit, reflecting the practical ease (Rukhsah) granted to travelers.
